summary: The US barred China's big phone carriers from getting American phone numbers directly, Beijing vowed a response, and Chinese cities are letting students start school a little later.
body: On Thursday the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which regulates phone and internet services, voted to stop China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom and other listed firms from getting US phone numbers directly for internet calling. The FCC says this is about national security and cutting scam robocalls.[^1][^2] Direct access is much cheaper for these firms; without it they would have to go through other providers.[^1] China's commerce ministry said it "firmly opposes" the vote, called it a push to cut US and Chinese telecom ties apart, asked Washington to reverse it and warned it would take countermeasures. It did not say what those would be.[^2]

Inside China, Chinese state media says the country has built 1,260 "5G factories", plants that run machines and sensors over fast 5G mobile networks, and is testing whether future 6G networks can also sense moving objects, which could help self-driving cars.[^3] Tech site The Next Web notes these figures come mostly from state media, do not match the industry ministry's own counts, and have not been checked independently; 6G is not expected in commercial use until about 2030.[^3]

Closer to a student's day: cities in Jiangsu province are pushing back school start times, with Jiangyin moving high schools to 7:20 a.m. from Nov. 5. One Nanjing parent said their child's day now runs 7:15 a.m. to 9:20 p.m., about 45 minutes shorter.[^4] Studies cited by Sixth Tone say Chinese high schoolers study around 68 hours a week, and about one in five 16- and 17-year-olds sleeps less than the official guideline. A Jiangsu education official called the problem severe.[^4] My read: later starts help, but sleep will only really improve if homework and evening study shrink too.
differences: On the phone numbers, the FCC calls the ban a security and anti-scam step; Beijing says it is really about splitting the two countries' telecom sectors.[^1][^2] On 5G factories, state media's counts differ from the industry ministry's, likely because they measure different things.[^3]

reads.title: Lesson in Endurance: China's Schools Start Later to Ease Burden on Students
reads.summary: How long Chinese high-school days really are, what the new later start times change, and why parents say homework still decides how much students sleep.
